title: Xor register: Boss receipt
topics: Recursion, sorting, binary search and bits
summary: Maintain a register initially 0. XOR each nonnegative reading into it and record the register after each reading. Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence.
descriptionMd:
A switch register toggles each indicated punch position as the ribbon advances. Alma adds numbered weights to the final receipt at the unit's inspection desk. The first derived reading has weight one, so its position matters as much as its value.

Maintain a register initially 0. XOR each nonnegative reading into it and record the register after each reading.

Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence.

Implement xorRegisterBossReceipt(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Prefix bit state. Maintain a register initially 0. XOR each nonnegative reading into it and record the register after each reading. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.

Target time O(n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with prefix bit state. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

Maintain a register initially 0. XOR each nonnegative reading into it and record the register after each reading. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.

Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence. Use an accumulator and a one-based position counter, revisiting the first level's loop work.

cases.explanation: The derived sequence is [7,4,3,3,15]. Its weighted products are [7,8,9,12,75]. Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence. This gives 111.

The derived sequence is [4,0,2,6]. Its weighted products are [4,0,6,24]. Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence. This gives 34.
